<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **3** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b1676441ba59cc32682ffd41e63e74474ad7fa42` → `packageMentionDocs`.

## Contract review

Head-sha: `4f4bb1fab759e516aee486e1d746806e354e3ebf`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/24765-team-sessions-related-list.md, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-session.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-team-derived-related-lists.test.ts + packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts (`FieldSchema.relatedList` describe :1696; `Field.lookup` :3158), packages/spec/liveness/field.json (`props.relatedList`), packages/platform-objects/src/identity/{sys-team-member,sys-invitation,sys-team}.object.ts and identity/index.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/pages/{sys-user,sys-organization}.page.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts (:753) and auth-schema-config.ts (:278), packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts (:602), packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/builtin-column-collision.ts (:136), packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.ts (:916), docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/{platform-core,identity-auth}.json, AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist step 3; the attribution rule), .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml (the Check Changeset job and its WHICH LEVEL prose) and ci.yml (concurrency :88-90; the Test Core aggregate :1463), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (launch-window header :58-100; level axis :1620-1700; `judgeLevel` :1760-1830), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (`CATEGORIES` :536; signals :676-684), every `.changeset/*.md` carrying `(narrowing)` (27 files), .changeset/pre.json and config.json, .claude/agents/os-dev.md (:42-55, :285-290, :400-401), the objectui checkout's packages/app-shell/src/utils/deriveRelatedLists.ts :283-302 at `2ec9e2a1a4` as a cross-check only (the pin is `12dc7b47c3`), card #24765 (body; comments 6285664872, 6289444669, 6289509411, 6290941965), PR #24881 (body, file list), the check-runs on this head read at 2026-10-20T12:48Z and the annotations of check-run 118628618615.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The narrowing — right.** The diff adds one key, `relatedList: false`, and one comment line to `sys_session.active_team_id` (sys-session.object.ts :237-238 on this head). The field is still `Field.lookup('sys_team', { label: 'Active Team', required: false, group: 'Context' })`: no lookup filter existed before or after, its label and column are untouched, and better-auth's write of `activeTeamId` still lands in `active_team_id` through `AUTH_ORG_SESSION_FIELDS` (auth-schema-config.ts :278), which the diff does not reach. `relatedList` is a presentation key on the server side: driver-sql classifies it `'presentation'` (builtin-column-collision.ts :136), so no DDL reads it; metadata-core's FLS projection lists it `keep` (object-schema-fls-references.ts :602), so the value reaches the console unchanged; lint only names it in a fix hint (data-model-rules.ts :916). No reader in packages/runtime, rest, mcp, objectql, plugins or metadata-core derives related lists (no `deriveRelatedLists`/`relatedLists` in any src), so no API or MCP door serves a team's related lists and nothing server-side reads the key as a list switch — the narrowing lands in the console alone, through the ledgered reader. `sys_team` declares no record page: plugin-auth registers only `SysOrganizationDetailPage` and `SysUserDetailPage` (auth-plugin.ts :753), and `packages/platform-objects/src/pages` holds only those two; sys-organization.page.ts :101 lists `sys_team` as a related list on the ORGANIZATION page, a different surface, unchanged. The session object's own list views (`all_sessions`, `mine`, `revoked`) and both actions are untouched, and `sys_team_member.team_id` (sys-team-member.object.ts :135) carries no `relatedList` key, so the Members list still derives — pinned.
- **The user's own Sessions list — unchanged, right.** `SysUserDetailPage` declares a `record:related_list` with `objectName: 'sys_session'`, `relationshipField: 'user_id'` (sys-user.page.ts :294-297); `sys_session.user_id` (sys-session.object.ts :174) carries no `relatedList` key; `revoke_my_other_sessions` stays at `locations: ['list_toolbar']` with its confirm text (:76-85) and `revoke_session` stays `list_item` (:88-93). The diff touches none of these; the three pins in the second `describe` read exactly these declarations.
- **The other lookups into `sys_team` — rightly left.** Every `lookup`/`master_detail` into `sys_team` in packages/ and examples/ is three: `sys_session.active_team_id` (fixed), `sys_team_member.team_id` (:135, the Members list, wanted) and `sys_invitation.team_id` (sys-invitation.object.ts :306, "Optional team to assign upon acceptance"). The Invitations list's toolbar action `invite_user` targets `/api/v1/auth/organization/invite-member` under `requiresMembershipReach: 'invite_member'` (:56-63) — organization-scoped, not caller-scoped; `accept_invitation`/`reject_invitation` are `list_item`/`record_header` with `visible: record.email == ctx.user.email` and `status == 'pending'` (:144-165) — invitee-only. A team-scoped list carrying an organization-scoped action is not this defect class.
- **The pins — right, one residual named.** `derivedRelatedLists(parent)` models the rule as: `type` in {`lookup`, `master_detail`}, `reference === parent`, `relatedList !== false`. That is the ledgered rule word for word: liveness/field.json `props.relatedList` is `live` with the evidence "deriveRelatedLists.ts:131 skips the FK entirely when relatedList is false", and `FieldSchema.relatedList`'s describe reads "false = suppress; true/absent = shown" (field.zod.ts :1696). The objectui checkout's deriveRelatedLists.ts :283-295 agrees line for line (skip unless `lookup`/`master_detail`; skip unless `reference === parentName`; skip when `relatedList === false`). `Field.lookup` emits `{ type: 'lookup', reference }` (field.zod.ts :3158-3163), so `field.type`/`field.reference` read as the pin expects; `SysSession`, `SysTeam`, `SysTeamMember` and `SysInvitation` are all named exports of the package index (identity/index.ts :11-20), so the CATALOGUE holds every lookup into `sys_team` this repo declares. Ablation judged from the code: without `relatedList: false,` the catalogue walk yields `sys_session.active_team_id` for `sys_team` (the `exclude sys_session` pin goes red) and `field.relatedList` reads `undefined` (the declaration pin goes red), while the three user-list pins read declarations the line does not touch — 2 failed | 3 passed, as claimed. Residual: objectui derives over the whole served registry while the pin walks this package's exports, so a lookup into `sys_team` declared by another package or an app sits outside its teeth; none exists in this repo, so this is a stated boundary, not a defect.

### ② Semver level

- **The level is `minor`; `patch` as written is wrong.** Three sources, one answer. (a) AGENTS.md step 3: "`(narrowing)` is BREAKING", and the launch-window convention (check-changeset-no-major.mjs :58-62, :72-80; the WHICH LEVEL prose in pr-automation.yml) reads "During the launch window we ship breaking changes as `minor`". (b) The gate on this head: Check Changeset (check-run 118628618615, completed 2026-10-20T12:34Z) is **failure** at step 15, "Guard against accidental major bumps (launch window)", on the level axis. Its annotation: "clause-② declares `no (narrowing)` while no moved package is graded `minor` or above … Moved and graded `patch`: @objectstack/platform-objects: patch (.changeset/24765-team-sessions-related-list.md) … direction arm: `narrowing` — a BREAKING change; during the launch window it ships `minor`". That is code, not prose: `judgeLevel` (:1808-1821) stands the axis down on `no` UNLESS the arm is `narrowing`, and then returns `enforce` → exit 1 when every moved package is `patch`. (c) Precedent: 27 changesets in `.changeset/` carry `(narrowing)`; 26 grade the narrowing package `minor`; the one patch-only file (24684) is on the private `@objectstack/example-showcase`, and the two that carry a `patch` beside a `minor` (24529, 24550) discharge the axis through that `minor`. The dev's open question is answered **B**.
- **Why the dev's local `check-changeset-no-major` exit 0 was not the verdict.** The axis reads the `Clause-②:` line from the `pull_request` payload (`--event` or `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`, :1623, :2408); with neither, the run takes the `no-pull-request` lane and exits 0 (verdict table :1683-1696). The declaration was only readable in CI, where it was read and refused. The dev's recommendation A rested on "both gates exit 0", which the local run could not measure; its "bump level is not the carrier" axis is true and still does not move the grade, because the convention and the gate fix a breaking change at `minor` for the window.
- **Declaration placement — right.** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is bare at the start of a line in the PR body (line 3) and in the changeset (line 7). The adr-0087 HTML-comment marker reads `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) …`, one marker, a category in `CATEGORIES` (:536-539); step 13 of Check Changeset is success and the annotation echoes the exemption text, and check-adr-0087-registration also reads the `(narrowing)` arm from the changeset as a breaking signal (:684). Read correctly.
- **The BREAKING banner — present, one prose defect.** `**BREAKING** for a reader of a team's derived related lists only …` with Before / Now / Unchanged / "What to do. Nothing." as the FROM / TO / Fix. AGENTS.md owes a FROM → TO mapping only when something an author can write is removed or renamed; nothing authorable moves here, so this form is sufficient and consistent with `no-migration-prescription` (the gate's R2 would refuse that exemption on a written prescription; none is written). Defect: the banner's sentence "Shipped as `patch` under the launch-window convention" misstates the convention, which ships breaking changes as `minor`, and this body ships verbatim into CHANGELOG.md. It must change with the grade.
- **Nothing widens.** +111/−0: one key the field was always free to set, one test file, one changeset. No export, type, spec key, route or stored shape moves.

- **Dependent suites narrowed (cli unit layer out at 585 s, declared to CI's Test Core) — answered, with a fact about this head.** The six Test Core shards on `4f4bb1fab7` did not conclude: `Test Core (1/6)`–`(6/6)` read `cancelled` at 2026-10-20T12:47Z, superseded when the branch moved (ci.yml :88-90 `cancel-in-progress: true`). The change is one presentation key no server code reads, so the unrun cli residue carries little risk, and the head that lands must have its shards concluded. Noted for the gate's owner, outside this card: an aggregate that reads `success` over six cancelled members.
- **`core test:repo` and the dependents ran on the pre-merge head `1e3f35f9a5` — answered.** The net diff of `4f4bb1fab7` against its merge-base `3fbef41b4a` is exactly the three files; the merge brought nothing into platform-objects or `relatedList`. Build Core, TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates and Governed Surface Queue Guard are green on this head; the pre-merge test evidence stands for the source the merge did not touch.
- **The PR attribution footer — not a deviation.** AGENTS.md (the attribution rule) makes an agent commit end with the model-free trailer pair and bans a model identifier from a PR body, a comment and a changeset; os-dev.md (:286, :290, :400-401) says the harness reminder yields and the PR body ends with the session-URL footer. All four branch commits carry exactly that pair, the PR body ends with the session-URL footer, and no model identifier appears in the title, body, commits or changeset. Compliant.
- **Open question 1 (changeset grade): B, `minor`** — see ②.
- **Open question 2 (a renderer-side pin in objectui): A, as shipped, is right.** The key is ledgered `live` with objectui's `deriveRelatedLists` as its evidence, so the cross-repo rule is already pinned where it is enforced; the spec-side pin models that rule and goes red the moment the declaration is dropped. Business need: no reader of a team's Sessions list exists. Long-term: the liveness ledger is the one place the cross-repo contract lives; a second pin in objectui would duplicate it. AI-error resistance: the spec pin already catches the regression this card is about. Focus: no sibling card for no newly measured risk.
- **The out-of-scope note (`sys_invitation.team_id`) — meets no filing gate.** os-dev.md :42-50 files only (a) a reproducible defect, (b) a breach of a declared contract, (c) a trap for AI-written metadata, each with a `reach:`. A team's Invitations list with an organization-scoped toolbar action and invitee-only row actions is a correct derived list: no wrong answer at a public door, no contract breached. "noted, not filed" is right.
- **The cross-lane surface — none, confirmed.** All three paths are `.changeset/` and `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/`, which is `domain:engine` (lane objection 6285664872 → relabel; claim 6289444669 under `domain:engine#1`). No objectui, cloud or services path is touched; no translation bundle moves (check-i18n-bundles in sync per the report, and CI's i18n lane is green).
